editorial:
Imagine you are stuck in a room with someone you can't stand, but you both have to work together to fight a demon. That is the basic setup here. You get two priests who are totally different. One is starting to doubt if God is even listening, and the other is running away from some pretty bad mistakes in his past. The vibe is heavy and tense, making you feel the pressure they are under. It is not just about the scary stuff; it is about whether these two men can actually trust each other before things go completely wrong.

The acting is the best part because you really feel their stress. The pacing starts slow but picks up speed once the exorcism begins, leading to a few shocks you won't see coming. While some of the dialogue feels a bit stiff, the tension makes up for it. If you enjoy stories about faith and fear, you should definitely check this out. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out the demon was actually feeding on the priests' guilt and doubt. The twist is that the exorcism only works when the two men finally forgive themselves and each other. Once they let go of their past mistakes, they gain the strength to cast the demon out for good. The movie ends with them surviving the night, though they are forever changed by the experience.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves supernatural thrillers and character dramas.
